summary.headline: Inflame Appliances H1 FY26 call: management guides to ~400,000 chimneys in next year, with Panchkula at 22,000/month and Hyderabad at ~50% utilisation.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY26 revenue grew over 40% with a sharp profit improvement, and said the H1 momentum would continue into H2. Monthly run rate is about 30,000–32,000 chimneys across Panchkula and Hyderabad, with November orders of 38,000–39,000 cited. Management is adding a multi-storey building at Panchkula (INR9–10 crore capex, bank debt sanctioned) targeted for 31 March, and is shifting to built-in and new products. No formal guidance on revenue or PAT was given; the chimney volume outlook for next year was stated only as a range of 350,000–500,000 units.

financial_highlights.value: 70.2% of raw material consumption (gross margin target 28–30%)
about 12%; PAT margin about 4.5% (interviewer-cited, not disputed)

segments.name: Chimneys
segments.commentary: Run rate above 30,000 units/month across both plants; Panchkula at about 22,000/month and Hyderabad at about 50% of capacity. Management expects chimney share of revenue to fall from 80–85% toward 60–65% by FY28.

segments.name: Hobs / built-in appliances (Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Hyderabad serves Crompton, IRB and KAFF with built-in refrigerators, wine coolers and built-in ovens. Hob volumes are expected to contribute meaningfully next year after BIS licensing; a customer has asked for 3,000–4,000 hob tops per month.

segments.name: New products (pipeline)
segments.commentary: Management plans 2–3 products that are currently imported from China, with a disclosure promised around 10–15 December after the CEO's China visit. Management also said these products are not yet Board-approved.

guidance_outlook: Chimney volume next year is not formally guided; management cited a range of 350,000–500,000 units and said 400,000 is a reasonable expectation (analyst's figure).
H2 FY26 run rate expected at about 30,000–35,000 chimneys/month, barring the lean months of April and post-Diwali.
Management targets 30–35% of revenue from non-chimney products in the next couple of years, and chimneys at no more than 60–65% by FY28.
Hyderabad utilisation expected to reach 80–90% within 5–6 months; both plants expected at similar margins and profitability by April–May 2026.
Management said it is aiming for 15% annual growth, and would like to sustain that year after year for the next 3–4 years.
Management declined to give PAT or revenue targets. It said it would revert on the company's total debt figure by email.
capex_capacity: Panchkula: multi-storey building (one floor for existing products, one for built-in products) with total capex of INR9–10 crore. Funded by bank debt, already sanctioned, with construction underway; target completion 31 March, with operations from 1 April.
Panchkula installed capacity to be expanded to 35,000–40,000 chimneys/month. Government approvals are pending, and management expects them to be cleared within about two weeks.
Temporary rental premises are being used for storage during construction. Management said there will be no plant shutdown.
Hyderabad capacity expansion is deferred until its utilisation reaches 18,000–20,000 chimneys/month; land and sheds are needed at a later stage.
Management said a third plant (Gujarat, export-focused, INR35–40 crore) is on hold; it wants to consolidate Panchkula and Hyderabad first.
Two small JVs with component specialists were set up with majority stakes held by the company.
demand_pricing: Monthly orders: April about 17,000–18,000; September about 45,000; November 38,000–39,000 across both plants. Actual production was 14,000–15,000 in April and more than 32,000 in September.
Management said the order book peaked at 60,000 in one month. Hindware volumes fell to 6,000–7,000/month from 10,000 earlier, and customers have asked for 7,000–8,000/month from April.
Chimney volumes for Havells rose from 3,000/month to about 7,000–8,000/month.
Management said Chinese CKD/SKD imports face BIS-related constraints, and no Chinese factory has BIS certification yet. It also said glass and cables must be sourced domestically.

Management said Chinese imports are priced below the price of local products, but its different hob route targets INR98 for a product that a CKD/SKD import would sell at INR120 (price comparison as stated).
Management said the Indian market for chimneys is around 1.6 million units, mostly imported earlier, though it said the question was now outdated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation at Hyderabad and Panchkula, and does the 6 lakh chimney capacity match the 30,000/month run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Panchkula is above 90% utilised (about 22,000/month) and Hyderabad about 50%, with 80–90% expected in 5–6 months. It said 100% utilisation is not realistic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding and capex for the new Panchkula building, and does it affect operations?
qa_highlights.answer: INR9–10 crore capex, funded by sanctioned bank debt; construction is underway. Temporary rental premises are being used for storage, and no shutdown is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order visibility for H2 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The current run rate is 30,000–32,000/month. Management expects about 30,000–35,000/month in H2 (barring October) and cited about 400,000 units for next year as a possible outcome.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and size of the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details will come in a disclosure around 10–15 December after the CEO's China visit. ASP and revenue details were not given; it said the board has not yet approved them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share outlook, and will the company launch its own brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to exceed 30% market share in a couple of years. It said there are no plans to launch chimneys under the company's own brand.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the total debt is outstanding and what are the working capital and asset turnover trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term borrowings were INR19.2 crore and short-term INR28.5 crore at 30 September. Management said the debtor balance includes LC bills under discount, and that working capital is comfortable.

risks_watch: Execution on the Panchkula expansion: government approvals and the 31 March completion target.
Hyderabad utilisation has to rise from about 50% to 80–90% to deliver the margin and volume targets.
Concentration risk with a few OEM customers, including Havells, Hindware, Crompton and KAFF. Hindware volumes have declined.
Pipeline products and hobs remain undisclosed and not yet Board-approved; the disclosure is expected mid-December.
Management stated a lean season in April and after Diwali, which affects quarterly volume comparisons.

Shareholding: the interviewer said promoter holding fell from about 61% to about 40% since March 2028 (as stated on call). Management attributed this to two fundraises and said there were no promoter sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on volumes, orders and the new products. Management was evasive on PAT and revenue targets, on the new product ASPs, and on the exact component imports. It was defensive on the shareholding change and on the warrant conversion.
key_quotes: Hyderabad plant is almost doing 50% now, whereas the Panchkula plant is almost at its peak.
No sir, we cannot afford to shut down our plant even for a day.
I think we are quite capable of reaching in excess of 30% in next couple of years.
So, next year Chimney -- percentage of Chimney revenue from Chimney sale will drastically drop down.

adds.what: Panchkula multi-storey building (INR9-10 crore, debt-funded, sanctioned) adding built-in products floor; Panchkula installed capacity to 35,000-40,000 chimneys/
Hyderabad capacity expansion (land and sheds), deferred until utilisation reaches 18,000-20,000 chimneys/month
Third plant in Gujarat, export-focused, INR35-40 crore

growth.why: Management aims for 15% annual growth sustained for 3-4 years and guides H2 run-rate of 30,000-35,000 chimneys/month, backed by Panchkula capex (INR9-10 crore, debt sanctioned, target 31 March) and spare Hyderabad capacity at ~50% utilisation, though no formal revenue or PAT guidance was given and new products are not yet Board-approved.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects Hyderabad utilisation to rise from about 50% to 80-90% within 5-6 months and both plants to reach similar margins by April-May 2026; manpower cost already down to about 10-11% of revenue from about 14%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Panchkula multi-storey building (INR9-10 crore, bank debt sanctioned, construction underway) targets 31 March completion with operations from 1 April, lifting Panchkula installed capacity to 35,000-40,000/month pending approvals expected within about two weeks.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Run rate is 30,000-32,000/month with H2 guided at 30,000-35,000/month and next-year range of 350,000-500,000 units (400,000 cited as reasonable); Hyderabad at about 50% gives spare room.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Panchkula near peak at about 22,000/month and Hyderabad at about 50%, so Hyderabad land and sheds are deferred until utilisation hits 18,000-20,000/month; the Gujarat INR35-40 crore plant is on hold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was confident on volumes and orders (November orders 38,000-39,000, peak 60,000 in one month), but gave no formal revenue or PAT guidance, so an upgrade is not yet anchored in numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Hindware volumes fell to 6,000-7,000/month from 10,000, concentration risk across few OEMs, and lean seasons in April and post-Diwali (October) could hit quarterly comparisons; Panchkula approvals and 31 March completion are execution risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 2-3 imported-from-China products and built-in/hob lines (customer asked for 3,000-4,000 hob tops/month), but these are not yet Board-approved and no ASP or revenue was given.

rows.label: Non-chimney revenue share to 30-35%
rows.why: Management targets chimneys at no more than 60-65% of revenue by FY28 from 80-85% now, which depends on built-in and hob products not yet Board-approved.

rows.label: Market share above 30%
rows.why: Management says it is capable of exceeding 30% share in a couple of years; the Indian chimney market is around 1.6 million units, and Havells volumes rose from 3,000 to 7,000-8,000/month.

rows.label: Panchkula government approvals
rows.why: Approvals are pending and management expects clearance within about two weeks; they gate the lift to 35,000-40,000/month capacity.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, orders and the 15% growth aim, but evasive on PAT and revenue targets, new product ASPs, and the shareholding change; analysts pushed on capacity utilisation, debt and the new products.

quality.why: Management stated H1 revenue grew over 40% and attributed it to chimney volume (run rate 30,000-32,000/month, Panchkula above 90% utilised, Hyderabad about 50%), but gave no split of price versus volume, no PAT or revenue figures, and no one-off items were disclosed in the brief.
